q: What are the emissions from boiling and drying turmeric per tonne?
title: Turmeric curing: emissions per tonne
short: Boiling is the energy step. Firewood or agricultural waste fires give biogenic CO2, reported separately, plus small methane and nitrous oxide amounts that do count. Steam boilers using coal or gas count fully. Sun drying adds nothing; mechanical dryers add their fuel or power.
audience: Turmeric growers, curing units and traders around Erode, Salem and Nizamabad, and spice exporters asked for product figures

ul: Fuel for boiling: firewood, dried leaves, coal or LPG, in kg or litres.
Electricity for polishers and dryers x 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh.
Diesel for transport to the yard or market.

p: CO2 from burning wood or crop waste is biogenic and shown outside the scopes. Methane and nitrous oxide from the fire are counted using IPCC defaults for the fuel.
Fresh rhizomes lose most of their weight in curing and drying. Report per tonne of dried, polished turmeric sold, and state it.
